A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sable research work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 45 MARL tasks, LBF and Neom scalability experiments, and ablations, with detailed results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and scalability results and additionally reports explicit comparisons involving Sable without temporal memory.

M1.justification: The retention architecture, episode resets, chunking procedures, objectives, and pseudocode remain unchanged. Cross-retention and the memoryless Sable configuration were already documented in v1's appendices; their greater prominence does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: The six benchmark suites and Neom patterns remain. Appendix A.3 revises the LBF scalability environments: the 32- and 64-agent grids change from 64×64 to 32×32 and 45×45, respectively, changing spatial density. The 128-agent scenario remains 64×64.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6a adds Sable without temporal memory to the RWARE/SMAX ablation comparison alongside Sable and the retained MAT variants. The main comparator set—MAT, MAPPO, IPPO, MASAC, HASAC, and QMIX—and its benchmark participation remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The expanded ablation explicitly contrasts full-history and current-timestep-only Sable. Appendix A.3 also revises grid-size controls to manage density during LBF scaling. The main training and evaluation budgets remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that the entire benchmark was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a targeted no-temporal-memory control on the same two RWARE and two SMAX tasks, testing whether history explains Sable's advantage over MAT. The existing normalization, gating, and chunk-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 independent trials, 95% confidence intervals, stratified bootstrap intervals for environment aggregation, and the same probability-of-improvement criterion. Additional result entries retain these reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds environment-level absolute-return aggregates in Table 1, including RWARE scores of 0.81 for Sable and 0.69 for MAT, plus memoryless ablation results. LBF 32- and 64-agent curves change under revised grid settings. Appendix Tables 2–6 retain their values, including all entries from v1's main Table 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, retention equations, losses, and worked decay-matrix examples match. v1 Equations 7–8 move to Appendix D.3.2 as v2 Equations 9–10. Expanded discussion of prior mirror-learning guarantees supplies no new formal result or proof for Sable.

C1.justification: The headline claims of 34/45 task wins, temporal context, memory efficiency, and scaling beyond a thousand agents remain. v2 adds an explicit contribution claim that its evaluations provide the first comprehensive results on the cited newly proposed JAX environment suites.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 refines the earlier attribution to retention plus long sequences: v2 identifies temporal memory specifically as the source of performance gains. Section 4.2 also qualifies the IPPO comparison by attributing its lower memory consumption to smaller networks.

D1.justification: v2 removes the scalability hyperparameter-transfer recipe and the explanation that tuning large tasks was infeasible. v1 identified the LBF 15x15-3p-5f task and three 16-agent Neom reference tasks. Appendix defaults, search spaces, hardware, pseudocode, and promised future code access remain.

R1.justification: v1's short related-work section becomes a substantially broader introduction covering independent learning, value factorization, actor-critic CTDE, heterogeneous-agent mirror learning, and offline sequence models. References such as VDN, QTRAN, QPLEX, and mirror learning are added, while focused Fast and Forgetful Memory and Linear Recurrent Unit references disappear.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten, with explicit evaluation criteria and contribution bullets. Related work is integrated into the introduction, and detailed decay-matrix exposition moves from the method section to Appendix D, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned around Sable versus MAT, a new MARL-spectrum diagram becomes Figure 2, and the main per-task table is replaced by an environment summary while its values remain in the appendix. Benchmark plots are enlarged, and scalability and ablation displays receive revised axes, curves, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: The added memoryless control in Section 4.3 strengthens the explanation of performance gains on the tested tasks. Expanded research positioning and clearer main-result displays also improve assessment of the contribution. These benefits provide a limited net improvement, tempered by the removal of useful hyperparameter-transfer details for reproducing the scalability experiments.
